To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a truncated mutant G-CSFR confers a strong proliferative advantage to hematopoietic stem cells in the presence of G-CSF via activation of Stat-5.
a truncated mutant Csr3r confers a strong HSC advantage that is dependent upon G-CSF and Stat5, and that the HSC advantage conferred by the Csr3r mutant is dependent on Stat5.
a truncated mutant G-CSFR confers a strong HSC advantage in mice that is mediated by Stat5 activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Stat5 in hematopoiesis.
the molecular basis of leukemic stem cell behavior.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the development of myeloid malignancies in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Csf3r mutations, which activate STAT5, confer a clonal advantage to HSCs and that the clonal dominance of HSCs in the BM of Csf3r mutant mice is due to activation of STAT5.
the G-CSF pathway, via Stat5, is a major regulator of the clonal dominance of HSCs expressing a truncated mutant G-CSFR.
the mutant Csf-3r receptor is a driver of clonal dominance in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Stat5 activation is required for the clonal advantage of HSCs that express mutant Csf3rs.

the Csf3r mutation is not sufficient to cause leukemia in the absence of G-CSF, but in the presence of G-CSF the mutant Csfr confers a strong proliferative advantage to the HSCs, which leads to a clonal dominance in the hematopoietic system.
the Csf3r mutation in mice confers the clonal advantage of HSCs via activation of Stat 5, and the Stat5 activation is critical for establishing clonal dominance of HSCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the G-CSF pathway is important for the clonal expansion of HSCs expressing a mutant G-CSF receptor.
the mutant Csf-3 receptor (CSF-3R) that is associated with human leukemia is also capable of conferring a strong clonal stem cell advantage in mice.
Stat5 signaling plays a key role for the clonal dominance of HSCs expressing a mutant Csf3R.
